alignments.note: Imperative rendered by the bare English imperative.
Substantival article before a participle: rule 32 gives it the pronoun *them* and nothing else; the relativizer and verb stay with the participle.

Participle rendered as a finite relative clause; *that* and *have* are rule 7 and 9 helpers on it. Rule 17's support-verb clause heads the unit on the meaning-bearing *rule*, not on *have*. The English *over* is not this unit's: no Greek preposition is expressed, so it realizes the bare genitive and rides with `ὑμῶν`, as at HEB.13.7 and HEB.13.24. Keeping *over* here was the competing reading and remains defensible — 1PE.5.3 `κατακυριεύοντες` → *lording it over* does exactly that, unhedged — but it cannot rest on the verb's compound prefix, which is not the corpus's test: EPH.5.7 `συμμέτοχοι` gives its *with* to the pronoun though `συμ-` stands, while the uncompounded `πεπίστευμαι` → *I had been intrusted with* at GAL.2.7 keeps its own particle.

Genitive complement of the participle: *over* realizes the bare case and rides with the pronoun, no Greek preposition being expressed and no article standing to anchor it, exactly as at HEB.13.7, HEB.13.17 and HEB.13.24 alike. 2CO.11.2 `ὑμᾶς` → *over you* reads a bare case the same way unhedged, and 2CO.1.24 is the same support-verb shape — `κυριεύομεν` → *we have lordship* with `πίστεως` → *over faith* — though hedged and conceding the other reading. That other reading is live and the corpus does not settle it: 1PE.5.3 `κατακυριεύοντες` → *lording it over* keeps *over* inside the verb's unit unhedged, and the corpus generally keeps a bare-case particle on an English phrasal verb, as `ἀνέχομαι` → *bear with* does in four units and as this chapter's own HEB.13.22 and HEB.13.14 *we seek after* do. I take the complement here because `ἡγέομαι` has no corpus unit of its own to follow and the nearest same-shape precedent is 2CO.1.24's *have + noun + over*, where the English preposition heads a phrase expressing the people ruled rather than being a particle the verb selects; reading it as the idiom's own particle remains defensible.
Expressed conjunction aligned to *and* in the ordinary way.

`ὑπείκω` takes a dative complement the Greek leaves unexpressed; the supplied *to them* is a rule 7 helper on the verb that requires it in English, as rule 74's contrast clause keeps a supplied object with its verb, and rule 11 keeps the ASV's italics from making it `added`. 2CO.3.14 folds an identical supplied *to them* and TIT.2.9 folds one onto `εὐαρέστους`. That the article `τοῖς` has already been spent on *them* two units earlier does not make this an `added` unit: rule 74 places a supplied object by which verb requires it, not by whether some other token has spent a like-sounding word, and rule 103's spent-token test is scoped to supplied **lexical** content, which a pronoun is not — rule 103 names a resumptive pronoun as its own contrast. 2CO.3.14 recorded the same situation hedged, so the reading that this *to them* is `added` is not foreclosed.
Postpositive `γάρ` rendered by the clause-initial *for*; rule 15 permits the reordering.
Emphatic nominative pronoun realized by the English subject.
Finite verb; the prepositional phrase after it belongs to `ὑπέρ` under rule 36.

Rule 67: the complex frame *in behalf of* rides undivided with the expressed preposition. `ὑπέρ` is a proper preposition, so rule 71 does not settle the head and rule 67 records the corpus as divided; I take the lexical noun *behalf* under rule 17, as EPH.5.32, PHP.1.5 and EPH.3.1 do. Heading on *in* with the 2 Corinthians run remains defensible.
Rule 20: the free genitive `ὑμῶν` supplies the English possessive *your*, displacing the article's determiner, so the article realizes nothing.
Head noun, bare after the possessive.
Genitive pronoun carrying the English possessive under rule 20.
Comparative adverb; no answering `καί` stands, so rules 82 and 100 are not in question.

Anarthrous future participle expanded into a finite relative clause; the supplied subject *they*, the relativizer *that* and the auxiliary *shall* are rule 7 and 9 helpers on it, and rule 9 heads the unit on the lexical verb.
Object noun, recoverable on its own English word (rule 2).
Rule 40: the subordinating conjunction takes whatever word introduces its English clause, here *that*.
Subjunctive with its supplied subject and modal auxiliary; rule 9 heads on the lexical verb *do*.
Substantival demonstrative object; no article stands with it, so rules 38 and 49 do not arise.
Preposition realized by *with*; rule 36 keeps it off the verb.
Anarthrous governed noun, its own English word.
Expressed conjunction aligned to *and*.
Ordinary negative `μή`, aligned to *not*. No negative indefinite follows, so rules 41 and 59 are not in question, and rules 44 and 64 are untouched, this being no interrogative particle.

One Greek participle rendered by a prepositional phrase; no Greek preposition stands for *with*, so it is a rule 7 helper inside the unit. Rule 66 heads on the meaning-bearing *grief*, which is what the ASV spends on the lexeme, rather than on the supplied preposition.
Postpositive `γάρ` rendered by the clause-initial *for*, as at s008; rule 15 permits the reordering.

Substantival demonstrative subject of the verbless clause, taking only *this*; the supplied copula goes to the adjectival predicate under rule 53. Rule 68's clause putting a substantival demonstrative on rule 53's pronoun side is the competing reading, but all its cited units have a **nominal** predicate, and rule 53's pronoun side is the noun-phrase exception; with an adjectival predicate rule 53's main principle applies, exactly as its own `ὅμοια` → *were like* and rule 68's own `Οὗτοι οἱ λόγοι` → *These* / *are faithful* do.
Predicate adjective of a verbless clause; rule 53 gives the supplied copula to an adjectival predicate, so *were* rides here rather than on the subject demonstrative.
Dative of disadvantage; the case preposition *for* rides with the pronoun under rule 21's determinerless clause, no article standing to anchor it.

review_notes: s003: *over* kept with the participle's own idiom rather than given to `ὑμῶν`; rule 36 governs an expressed Greek preposition, and none stands here.
s010: rule 67's genuinely divided case for a proper preposition — head taken on *behalf* with the EPH/PHP reading; the 2CO reading on *in* is defensible and named in the note.
s025/s028: the supplied *were* is placed on the adjectival predicate under rule 53 rather than on the demonstrative subject under rule 68; the competing reading is named in s028's note.
